title: 'The G Engines Are Coming' article arrives on Cook's desk

tellings.quote: there was an article that showed up on my desk. I mean, people would send stuff to us at Jane's.
there's a really interesting article from 1956 called the G engines are coming or something like that.
tellings.difference: Leaves out Cook and credits Gladish, Deser and Arnowitt instead of Trimble.
tellings.link_reason: The same 1956 'The G Engines Are Coming' article as the story where it reaches Cook at Jane's.

plain: The story is that a 1956 article titled 'The G-Engines Are Coming' shows that America's aviation industry was openly chasing antigravity engines in the 1950s. Nick Cook, a journalist at the defence magazine Jane's, tells Michels that the article simply turned up on his desk, since people would send material to Jane's. He ties it to a man named George S. Trimble. Michels brings up the same article in another episode and links it to Michael Gladish and to the physicists Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt, without mentioning Cook. If the article means what they take it to mean, antigravity work began decades ago and then went quiet.
